In Williamson County, deeds and other real property records are recorded by the county clerk, and the clerk's page lists where to search them. This guide gives the office details and recording rules we could confirm on official pages. We did not confirm every fee or hour, and we say where we could not.

Where to find Williamson County property records

The Williamson County clerk's page describes Official Public Records covering land titles, liens, releases of liens, plats, IRS liens, trusts, security agreements, restrictions and notices.

  • Office: County Clerk.
  • Address: 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626 (recording and vital records).
  • Phone: 512-943-1515.
  • Hours: Research Library, Recording and Vitals: 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
  • Online records search: official records search.

The clerk's office says it does not perform searches for the public.

What Texas law says about recording

The county clerk serves as the county recorder, and deeds and other instruments are recorded in the county where the property is located (Local Government Code Sec. 191.001). The clerk must correctly record instruments that are proved, acknowledged or sworn to, in the order filed (Property Code Sec. 11.004).

A deed for real property executed after December 31, 1981 must show a mailing address for each grantee, or the filer pays a penalty fee equal to the greater of $25 or twice the statutory recording fee (Sec. 11.003). See Texas property records and the warranty deed and quitclaim deed guides.

Harris County by the numbers

Where do you record a deed or lien release in Harris County?

The Harris County Clerk's Real Property Department records documents tied to real estate, and it will accept anything a statute authorizes, requires and permits to be filed. In person, go to 201 Caroline, 3rd Floor, Suite 320, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The department's phone number is (713) 274-8680.

Plan to arrive early. Everyone entering the building passes through security, the door to Suite 320 locks promptly at 4:30 p.m., and you must be inside before 4:00 p.m. to get a non-certified copy. Because Harris County has more than 3.3 million residents, the clerk may require a photo ID from a person filing in person, and the clerk's page says each filer must show their own government-issued identification.

Releases of lien can also go to the annex offices, but the clerk warns that those can take five to seven business days to reach the downtown office. For a closing on a deadline, file downtown or use e-recording.

Can you mail or e-record a document to the Harris County Clerk?

Yes to both, with limits. Mailed originals go to the clerk's Attn: Real Property Department at P.O. Box 1525, Houston, TX 77251-1525, and the postal service delivers only to that box. Couriers with a tracking number use 201 Caroline, 4th Floor, Suite 460 on weekdays.

Mail payment must be a cashier's check, a money order or an approved business or firm check drawn on a U.S. bank. The clerk does not take cash or personal checks by mail, and it rejects temporary, estate, trust or association checks and any check with mark-outs.

E-recording must run through an approved provider. The clerk's page names Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network and Simplifile as examples. Texas law limits who may e-file to groups such as licensed attorneys, banks and credit unions, title insurance companies and agents, state agencies and municipal clerks. A document queued before 2:00 p.m. central time is processed the same business day, and anything later waits until the next one.

What does Harris County charge to record real property?

The clerk's real property fee schedule lists a handful of base charges, shown below as printed. A deed with a few pages and no more than five names to index sits at the low end of the range.

Harris County Clerk real property fee schedule
ChargeAmountSource

Each additional page$4.00Same page
Each name over five indexed$0.25Same page

Plain paper copy$1.00 per pageSame page

The office raised its records management and archive fees from $6.00 to $10.00. A condominium declaration is recorded at $10.00 per taped sheet, and each key map page attached to a condo filing is $50.

What does the Harris County Clerk require on a document before accepting it?

The clerk accepts only original documents or certified copies of court documents, and a photocopy will not be recorded. A rejected filing costs time, so check the list before you send anything.

  • The signer's signature must be an original and must be notarized, except for an IRS release.
  • Names are printed under every signature, with the capacity of the signer and the entity named.
  • The document needs legal descriptions where they apply and a printed return address.
  • Leave a margin of 1 to 2 inches across the top and left side for recording information.
  • A conveyance must show each grantee's address, or the filer pays the greater of $25 or twice the recording fee.
  • An abstract of judgment must show the plaintiff's mailing address.

An original will cannot be filed in the real property records. A will goes to the Probate Department for safekeeping, and a probated will can be recorded as a certified copy issued by the probate court. A will can also be attached as an exhibit to an affidavit of heirship.

How do you get copies of Harris County property records and guard against fraud?

The clerk's eCommerce feature lets the public buy certified and non-certified copies of recorded documents, and the Public Records Department at 713-274-6390 answers questions about it.

The clerk also offers the free Property Alert System, which notifies homeowners when a new real property document is filed under their name. Owners who rent out a house, who have heirs, or who have a title question should sign up before listing, since an unexpected filing is easier to fix before a buyer finds it.

Value and ownership for tax purposes come from the Harris Central Appraisal District at hcad.org. A title company reads these records for liens, judgments and unresolved heirs, and a sale usually pauses until each item is released or paid.

Which recorded documents decide how fast a Harris County sale can close?

A title company reads the chain of recorded papers, and each type has its own home in the clerk's files. Gaps are most common after a death or a missed mortgage payment.

  • After an owner dies, the route depends on the estate: an executor's or administrator's deed for an administered estate, a court order plus the will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship when neither applies.
  • A transfer on death deed only works if it was recorded before the owner died, and the recorded affidavit of death and the death certificate follow it.
  • A foreclosure sale notice must be filed with the clerk and posted at the courthouse at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction, which the state sets between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
  • A deed of trust is cleared by a recorded release of lien, which the clerk accepts downtown and at annexes.

The Texas State Law Library notes that a county cannot rewrite an old deed to add heirs, so the fix is a new recorded instrument. Start the paperwork before listing the house, because an affidavit or court order can take longer to arrange than the sale itself.

How large is the Harris County housing market?

Harris County is the most populous county in Texas: the July 2025 estimate is 5,045,026 people, up from 4,731,145 at the 2020 census. It spans 1,706.96 square miles of land and counted 2,012,848 housing units, and 30,909 building permits were issued in 2025.

Owners live in 54.7 percent of homes, and renters have the rest. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau lists a median home value of $276,600, a median rent of $1,401 and a median household income of $74,983. People 65 and older are 13.1 percent of residents, 26.8 percent were born abroad, and 151,833 are veterans.

A county this large produces a large volume of recorded documents, from deeds of trust to liens to affidavits of heirship. That volume is one reason the clerk insists on clean originals, precise fees and approved e-recording vendors.

More questions about Harris County, TX Property Records

Where is the Harris County Clerk's real property office?

The in-person counter is at 201 Caroline, 3rd Floor, Suite 320, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Real Property Department's phone number is (713) 274-8680.

Does the Harris County Clerk require a photo ID to file?

Yes, for in-person filing. Texas law lets a clerk in a county of 3.3 million or more require photo identification, and the clerk's page says each person must present their own valid government-issued ID.

Can I record a copy of my deed in Harris County?

No. The clerk accepts original documents with original signatures, or certified copies of court documents. Photocopies of a deed will be refused.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Harris County?

The posted schedule is $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each added page, $0.25 for each name over five, plus a $10.00 archive fee and a $10.00 management fee. Check the clerk's page for the latest amounts.

How do I get alerts when someone files a document under my name?

Sign up for the Harris County Clerk's free Property Alert System. It notifies homeowners of any new real property document filed under their name.

Dallas County by the numbers

Where are Dallas County property records kept?

Deeds, mortgages, releases and other land records for Dallas County sit with the County Clerk's Recording Division in the Records Building at 500 Elm Street, Suite 2100, Dallas, TX 75202. The division describes itself as the recorder of deeds and keeper of the Official Public Records.

By the clerk's own count the office records roughly 400,000 documents a year. That stream includes deeds, liens against a property, transfers between owners, probate papers that touch land, and the release of lien filed once a mortgage is paid off. The stated purpose is to tell the public who holds a financial interest in a parcel.

  • Phone: (214) 653-7099
  • Hours: opens 8:00 a.m., closes 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, with court-approved holidays excepted
  • Mail: Dallas County Clerk's Office, Recording Division, 500 Elm Street, STE 2100, Dallas, Texas 75202
  • Questions the FAQ page does not answer: recording@dallascounty.org

Anyone selling a house in Dallas County will touch this office through the title company, since the title search and the filing of the new deed both run through these records. The clerk's Recording Division page is the place to start.

How do I search and copy Dallas County records?

Start with the clerk's Online Public Record Search, which returns non-certified images, then buy a certified copy only if a lender, court or title company asks for one. The clerk states plainly that the free search and the certified service are two different things.

Certified electronic copies of Official Public Record documents are sold on the clerk's website around the clock. Each one carries the clerk's digital signature and tamper-proof encryption, so a buyer's lender can accept it without a paper original. In person or by mail, the clerk prices real property copies at $1.00 per page for a plain copy, and $1.00 per page plus a $5.00 certification fee per document for a certified one.

Plat copies are priced separately: $6.00 per page for the large 18 by 24 size and $1.00 per page for 8.5 by 11, with the same $5.00 per-plat certification fee on certified copies. The clerk keeps only the plats filed with that office, so a subdivision map recorded elsewhere will not be there.

Recorded deeds sometimes carry a Social Security number, driver's license number, date of birth or bank account number. Under House Bill 2061, the clerk says that kind of information may be eligible for redaction. The owner files a Redaction Request Form by mail or in person. Once a document is recorded, any other change needs a later filing, and the clerk suggests asking a lawyer whether a correction document or a fresh deed is the right fix.

What are the Dallas County Clerk's recording charges?

The first page of a standard document costs $25.00 and every page after it costs $4.00. The clerk breaks the first-page charge into $5.00 for recording, $10.00 for records preservation and $10.00 for archiving.

Certification added to a copy$5.00 per document

Any writing on the back of the last sheet is billed as a full $4.00 page, so a signature block that spills onto a reverse side costs the same as a new page. The clerk also lists specialty documents with their own fees, and a few filings, such as child support liens and military discharge papers, carry no filing fee.

Payment rules are strict. The office takes cash, money orders, cashier's checks and business checks made out to the Dallas County Clerk, and it does not accept personal checks. Cards work only in person, with a 2.05 percent convenience fee on credit and pinless debit or $2.85 on pin debit. The fee page adds that filings sent by mail need a self-addressed stamped envelope for the file-stamped copy.

What does the Dallas County Clerk require before recording a deed?

The deed has to be signed and properly acknowledged, and for deeds conveying property between people the clerk now asks for a photo ID. Under House Bill 1195, photo ID has been required since July 1, 2023 on documents that convey property from one person to another.

  • Acknowledgment. A deed can be recorded only if it is acknowledged or sworn before an authorized officer such as a notary, or witnessed by two subscribing witnesses, according to the Texas county clerk manual.
  • Court-ordered papers. A document that comes from a court action must be a certified copy authenticated by the court or its clerk.
  • Grantee address. The manual notes that a missing grantee mailing address can add a $25 charge.
  • Notary on site. The FAQ says a notary sits on the fourth floor in the Treasurer's office from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. daily for $10, cash only.
  • Electronic filing. Local Government Code Sec. 195.003 limits e-recording to attorneys, banks and credit unions, federally approved lenders, licensed regulated lenders, licensed title insurers and agents, and state agencies.

That last point matters for owners selling without an agent. An individual who is not on the list files on paper at the Elm Street counter or by mail, or lets the title company submit the deed electronically after closing.

What do Dallas County's numbers mean for a seller?

Dallas County has a lower owner-occupied rate than Denton County (65.5 percent) or Ellis County (75.8 percent), and that shapes the mix of sales. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page puts the owner-occupied rate at 50.8 percent for 2020 to 2024, so roughly half of households rent. A seller whose house is leased out should expect a buyer or title company to ask for the lease and tenant details.

The same page lists a July 2025 population estimate of 2,661,397, up 1.9 percent from the 2020 base, spread over 873.06 square miles of land and 1,099,775 housing units. The 2020 count was 2,613,539 people, or 2,993.6 per square mile. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $303,000, median gross rent is $1,565, and median household income is $76,547 in 2024 dollars. Builders pulled 12,691 permits in 2025.

Median monthly owner costs run $2,166 with a mortgage and $793 without one. That gap shows up at a closing table: a house with no mortgage is simpler to transfer because there is no lender payoff and no release of lien to track down.

Which record problems slow a Dallas County sale?

Unreleased liens, unfiled estate paperwork and tax debts cause most of the delays, and all of them show up in the records the clerk keeps. A title company runs the search before closing and flags what it finds.

  • Old mortgages. A paid-off loan should have a recorded release of lien. If none was filed, the lender has to be contacted to issue one.
  • Tax liens. State and federal tax lien notices are filed with the clerk, and the clerk lists fixed fees for both and for their releases.
  • Foreclosure notices. A notice of sale is posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk, usually at least 21 days before the sale, according to the Texas State Law Library.
  • Estates without a clean chain. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, and the State Law Library says no law forces a third party to accept it. A court order or probate may be needed instead.
  • Hospital and child support liens. Both appear on the clerk's fee page and have to be cleared if they attach to the property.

If any of these turn up, ask the title company which instrument cures the problem and who files it.

How do property taxes affect closing on a Dallas County house?

Property tax is a lien on the land from January 1 of each year, and the Comptroller says the person who owned the property that day is liable for that year's bill. A sale in November does not erase the lien; it just shifts who pays it at closing.

Texas bills usually go out around October 1, and taxes unpaid on February 1 become delinquent. The Comptroller prints a six percent penalty and one percent interest on that day, with the penalty growing by one percent each month until July 1. People over 65 or disabled can pay in installments. Ask the Dallas County tax office for the current balance, and ask the county appraisal district whether a homestead exemption is on file, since a buyer who takes the house after January 1 may be able to claim one for the rest of that year if the seller did not.

More questions about Dallas County, TX Property Records

What is the first-page charge for a deed at the Dallas County Clerk?

The first page costs $25.00 and each additional page costs $4.00. The first-page fee is built from $5.00 for recording, $10.00 for records preservation and $10.00 for archiving. Information on the back of a page is charged as a full page.

Can I pay Dallas County recording fees with a personal check?

No. The clerk accepts cash, money orders, cashier's checks and business checks payable to the Dallas County Clerk. Cards are taken only in person, with a 2.05 percent convenience fee on credit and pinless debit cards or $2.85 on pin debit.

Are the documents in the online public record search certified?

No. The clerk says online search results are non-certified. A separate service sells electronic certified copies with the clerk's digital signature, and paper certified copies cost $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document.

Can I e-record my own deed in Dallas County?

Usually not. Local Government Code Sec. 195.003 limits electronic recording to attorneys, banks, certain lenders, title companies and state agencies. An individual owner normally files on paper at 500 Elm Street or has a title company file the deed.

How do I remove a Social Security number from a recorded Dallas County document?

Submit a Redaction Request Form to the County Clerk's Office by mail or in person. The clerk says House Bill 2061 makes certain personal data, including Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, dates of birth and account numbers, eligible for redaction.

  • Office: County Clerk.
  • Address: Deed Records are handled at the Paul Elizondo Tower, San Antonio.

What Texas law says about recording

Bexar County by the numbers

Which Bexar County office records deeds and liens?

The Bexar County Clerk's Recordings Division files and maintains real property records, personal property records, notices of trustee sale and public notices. Filing in person happens at the Paul Elizondo Tower, 101 W. Nueva, Suite 103, San Antonio 78205, phone 210-335-2581. A Southside Annex inside Precinct 1 at 3505 Pleasanton Rd. also takes filings, at 210-335-3522.

The doors are open weekdays from 8 a.m., closing at 5 p.m. except Wednesdays, when the office stays open until 5:45. Deed Records, the desk that pulls copies and researches liens, is in Suite B109 of the same tower at 210-335-2273. Mail goes to the Clerk's Office, Attn: Recordings, 100 Dolorosa, Suite 104, San Antonio.

The clerk's site lists a "Records on the Run" satellite office that rotates through precinct offices and community centers each month, so a filer can skip the downtown trip. The clerk also runs a Vanguard Property Alert that warns owners about potentially fraudulent filings, and accepts wills for safekeeping.

What are Bexar County's fees for filing a deed?

Filing a one-page instrument with the Bexar County Clerk costs $25.00, and every added page is $4.00. The first-page charge breaks into a $5.00 recording fee, a $10.00 records archive fee and a $10.00 records management fee, all effective January 1, 2024.

Pages in the documentTotal fee in Bexar County

Source: Bexar County Clerk, Real Property Recording Fees, which lists every total from 1 through 50 pages.

The same page lists the add-ons you are most likely to meet:

  • Notice of trustee sale: $2.00 filing, $1.00 for a plain copy
  • Federal tax lien instruments: $30.00 total
  • Plats: $81.00 total per mylar
  • Deed copies: $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per certification
  • Electronic copy of an electronic document: $1.00 up to 10 pages, then $0.10 per page

What are the filing rules for Bexar County recordings?

The clerk records only originals with original signatures and will not record a copy. Documents are cashiered, given an instrument number and scanned on the spot, then the originals are handed back or returned. Payment can be cash, credit card, check or money order, with checks written to the Bexar County Clerk.

Electronic filing is a separate lane. Section 195.003 of the Local Government Code limits it to attorneys, banks and credit unions, federally backed mortgage lenders, persons approved to make regulated loans, title companies, state agencies and municipal clerks. The clerk lists six approved e-filing providers, among them CSC, Simplifile, ePN, Indecomm and Hopdox.

The clerk's staff do not draft deeds and do not vouch for a clear title, and they send people who want assurance to title companies and attorneys. A conveyance also has to be signed and acknowledged before a notary or similar officer before it can go on record, a rule the Texas county clerk manual ties to Property Code 12.001(b).

How can a seller check for liens on a Bexar County house?

Start with the clerk's public records search, or visit the Deed Records Department in Suite B109 of the Paul Elizondo Tower, where staff can point you to recorded liens against a property. The clerk does not guarantee clear title and takes no responsibility for encumbrances, so a guaranteed search comes from a title company, with an attorney as the other route.

Mortgage foreclosure notices can be pulled from the same search. A list is also available through the clerk's GIS Foreclosure Map or at the Deed Records counter, while the list of tax foreclosures comes from the law firm that handles them at 210-225-4422.

  • Release of lien: record the original in person at the tower or mail it to the courthouse office, at $25.00 for the first page
  • Lost deed: a certified copy runs $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per certification
  • Plain copies: found online under Land Records in the Official Public Records Search

How do foreclosure sales work in Bexar County?

Mortgage and tax foreclosure sales in Bexar County are public cash auctions held the first Tuesday of each month between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. When that Tuesday falls on January 1 or July 4, the sale moves to Wednesday. Per the clerk, bidding happens outdoors beside the courthouse, in the gap between it and the Paul Elizondo Tower, unless Commissioners Court names a different spot.

Bidders need no registration for a mortgage foreclosure, but registration is required to bid on a tax foreclosure. Only cash or certified funds work, and personal checks are refused. A GIS Foreclosure Map tracks notices and is refreshed twice a month, on the first Friday after the auction and about 18 days before the next sale.

Redemption periods are stated on the clerk's page: two years for agricultural or homestead property and six months for other property, counted from the day the sale deed goes on record. The clerk also hosts a free foreclosure training seminar on the first Tuesday of each month. The State Law Library adds that a notice of sale must be posted and placed on file with the clerk 21 or more days ahead.

How big is Bexar County, and what does its housing look like?

Bexar County spans 1,248 square miles around San Antonio, which serves as both seat and biggest city. The Handbook of Texas places it along the Balcones Escarpment, with hilly Edwards Plateau country in the northwest and flatter prairie and South Texas plains elsewhere. The San Antonio River and the Medina River drain it, and Interstates 10, 35, 37 and 410 plus U.S. 281 and U.S. 90 carry traffic through.

Bexar was established as a county on December 20, 1836. The mission-era area around the Alamo and the five Spanish missions is part of the historic record behind many older lots, and military bases, tourism, medical centers and higher education drive the present economy. Suburbs include Alamo Heights, Converse, Universal City, Terrell Hills and Castle Hills.

Who keeps property records in Denton County?

The County Clerk's Recording Division keeps every real property record for Denton County, along with vital statistics. Its physical and mailing address is 1450 E. McKinney Street, Denton, TX 76209, and the office keeps weekday hours, from 8 in the morning to half past four.

The county runs six County Clerk locations, and all of them offer passport acceptance. Real property filings are different: the county states that every recording must be sent to the Denton location, so a seller in another part of the county cannot drop a deed at a branch office.

  • By mail: Denton County Clerk, Attn: Recording, 1450 E. McKinney St., Denton, TX 76209
  • Electronically: through one of the clerk's listed electronic recording partners

Anyone who files by USPS, FedEx or UPS has to include the right request and payment form. The clerk's Recording Division page explains the mail-in route and links the e-recording partners.

How are recordings submitted to the Denton County Clerk?

Paper filings reach the Denton office through the mail or at the counter, and electronic filings must go through an approved partner. The county says you need to choose one of those partners before submitting any electronic recording, and each partner can explain its own process.

Mailed packets can be paid with a business check, money order, cashier's check or a credit card, and the card has to be entered on the clerk's Credit Card Payment Form. Over the counter, the fee page also lists cash. The county does not list personal checks among accepted forms of payment.

For a copy of something already recorded, the clerk's schedule charges $5 for a clerk's certificate, when one is needed, plus $1 for each page or part of a page. A records search done by clerk staff is $10 per entry. A title company usually orders its own copies, so an owner who only needs the deed can ask the title officer before paying for a certificate.

What are the Denton County recording fees?

Denton County prints a $25 first-page fee and adds a required recording information page at $4, then $4 for each page after that. The schedule lists the information page as its own line item, so a deed that looks like a single page on paper is still priced for more than one.

Denton County is growing quickly and its housing is newer and pricier than most of Texas. Census QuickFacts lists a July 2025 estimate of 1,069,346 residents, an 18.0 percent rise on the 2020 base of 906,530 and well above the 662,614 counted in 2010.

Pull the vesting deed, the deed of trust and any releases, then compare the names and legal description against what the tax records show. Mismatches are easy to fix before an offer and slow to fix after one.

  • Liens. A state tax lien, federal tax lien or unreleased mortgage will be visible in the clerk's index, and the schedule lists a fee for each filing and for the federal release.

The last day to pay without penalty is January 31; February 1 starts delinquency. The collector then adds six percent penalty and one percent interest, with the penalty rising to 12 percent on July 1. Homeowners age 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans can pay in four installments.

Texas has no state property tax, so every dollar of the bill comes from local units such as the county, school district and city. Ask the Denton County tax office for the current balance before closing, and ask the appraisal district to confirm any homestead, over-65 or disabled veteran exemption on file. Who records property documents in Hidalgo County?

The Hidalgo County Clerk is the county's recorder, and the clerk's Recording Department files deeds, liens and judgments. The clerk's page says county land records can be searched, viewed, printed and downloaded through the website. Under the state constitution the clerk acts as "Recorder of the County," and the county's Recording page lists four tasks for each instrument: decide whether it will be accepted, file it, record it and index it.

Documents handled in the Recording Department include warranty deeds, trustee's deeds, tax liens, state and federal, foreclosures, judgments, subdivision plats and financing statements. The same department processes assumed name certificates, and since September 1, 2017 a county clerk may waive the fees for a military veteran who files one or files a statement of abandonment. The clerk's office also keeps court records, vital records, marriage licenses and probate files, so one trip to the clerk can cover several parts of an estate sale.

Hidalgo County covers 1,570.96 square miles of land according to the Census Bureau, so confirm with the clerk's office which counter or online route fits your filing before you travel.

How do I search Hidalgo County official records?

The clerk's Official Records Search sends you to the county's online records portal at hidalgo.tx.publicsearch.us. The county describes its land records as searchable, viewable, printable and downloadable from the website.

Search with a checklist. Ahead of a listing or a signed contract, pull these items:

  • The vesting deed that put the current owner on title.
  • Every deed of trust, with a recorded release for each loan that was paid.
  • Tax liens, judgments and foreclosure postings under the owner's name.
  • Any plat or subdivision record that affects lot lines or easements.

Run every spelling variation of each owner's name, including hyphenated and compound surnames and middle names. A single missed spelling can hide an old lien until a title company finds it. Repeat the search shortly before closing.

What does Hidalgo County charge to file a deed?

The clerk's fee schedule page prints $35 for page one of an instrument going into the Official Public Records, then $4 per extra page. It also explains that Senate Bill 1612 repealed a $1.00 document filing fee, which the clerk removed from official public records recordings, assumed names, foreclosure notice postings, plats and marriage licenses. The page is titled as the 2024 schedule, so call the clerk to confirm the current figure before sending payment.

The statewide clerk manual shows a recording charge as a stack of parts: a base amount per page plus separate records management, archive and technology fees, and a $25 add-on when no grantee mailing address appears. Counties combine these differently, so the Hidalgo schedule is the one to follow for a Hidalgo filing.

A deed gets accepted only when the signer acknowledged it in front of a notary or comparable officer, or swore to it before two witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). File it in the county that contains the parcel.

How big is the Hidalgo County housing market on paper?

Hidalgo County has a big household base and a middle home value of $140,900, which means a small lien can swallow a large share of a seller's equity. The table gives the federal figures.

Hidalgo County snapshot from the federal QuickFacts page

The federal tables show 270,210 households and 19,401 veterans, with 24.2 percent of residents below the poverty line. Where a house is a family's main asset, an unpaid tax bill or a deed signed by one relative only can stall a sale. A house that passes through several relatives without a probate case leaves a gap in the record chain that a buyer's title company will ask you to close.

Who values and taxes a Hidalgo County house?

The Hidalgo County Appraisal District, created on January 1, 1980, appraises property and administers exemptions for the county's taxing units. An eight-member board appointed by the taxing units governs it, and the county assessor-collector sits on the board as a voting member. Cities, school districts, utility districts and the county each set their own rate, and the district's values feed all of them.

Across Texas, value is fixed as of January 1, which is also the day the tax lien attaches. Bills go out around October 1 and turn delinquent on February 1, when a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added. An owner who disagrees with a value can protest, and the usual cutoff is mid-May.

The district's public portal offers property valuations, tax information and online filing of appeals and exemptions. A homestead owner can claim the $140,000 school district exemption, and seniors and disabled owners receive another $60,000 for school tax. Homestead appraisals may rise no more than 10 percent a year once the exemption is first granted.

What record issues come up in Hidalgo County sales?

Four situations come up often: heirs, contract for deed sales, old liens and unpaid tax. Each leaves a trail at the clerk's office, and each is easier to fix before a buyer's title company finds it.

  • Heirs without a probate case. A will can be probated within four years of death, and a muniment of title order lets that will carry title when no administration is needed. The small estate affidavit route covers estates of $75,000 or less, leaving out the homestead and exempt property.
  • Contract for deed. Under Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D, a seller who keeps title on a residential contract owes the buyer an annual statement each January, and the buyer has a statutory right to cancel in set time frames.
  • Unreleased deeds of trust. A paid loan with no recorded release still clouds title.
  • Delinquent tax. Seniors and disabled owners may pay in four installments, and some collectors allow plans up to 36 months on a homestead.

Several of these fixes take weeks, so begin early. A lender can be asked for a release, a probate filing goes through the clerk's probate staff, and a tax balance is paid to the collector. Whichever item the title company says blocks closing goes to the front of the line.

If you are not sure which record is the problem, ask the clerk's Recording Department to confirm what is indexed under the owner's name, then bring the results to a title company.

More questions about Hidalgo County, TX Property Records

Where do I find a Hidalgo County deed?

Search the clerk's official records portal at hidalgo.tx.publicsearch.us, or ask the County Clerk's Recording Department. Hidalgo County says its land records can be searched, viewed, printed and downloaded online.

What is the filing charge for a deed in Hidalgo County?

Hidalgo's fee page lists $35 for the opening page and $4 for every page after it, on a schedule titled 2024. Verify the present amount with the clerk's office before filing.

Is the appraisal district the same as the county clerk?

No. The Hidalgo County Appraisal District sets values and administers exemptions, and the County Clerk records deeds and liens. They keep separate records, so a recorded deed does not by itself change a homestead exemption.

Can heirs sell a Hidalgo County house without probate?

Sometimes. A transfer on death deed on record before the owner died, or a small estate affidavit for an estate of $75,000 or less (homestead and exempt property excluded), can move title without full administration. The buyer's title company decides whether to accept the paperwork.

What does a contract for deed change about my record?

The seller keeps title until the buyer pays in full, so the recorded deed still shows the seller. The annual January statement and the buyer's right to cancel come from Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D.

Plat or map, first page$70.00
Posting public notices$2.00

The sheet also prices plat pages after the first at $25.00 each, UCC financing statements at $35.00 or $50.00 when they run three pages or more, and hospital liens at $25.00. Veterans filing an assumed name certificate pay nothing.

A notice of sale for a foreclosure is posted at the $2.00 notice fee. Under the Texas county clerk manual, a notice has to appear at the courthouse and be filed with the clerk.

How do I pay and get copies at the Ellis County Clerk?

The clerk accepts checks made out to the Ellis County Clerk and charges a processing fee on cards. Card and debit transactions carry a 2.4 percent fee, with a $1 minimum. A returned check costs $25.00, and the office will not take a check more than 90 days old. Refunds wait until a check has cleared the bank.

Copy fees are modest and are set under Local Government Code Sec. 118.0145. A noncertified paper copy is $1.00 for each page or part of a page, and so is a paper document converted to electronic form. An electronic copy of an electronic document is $1.00 for a document up to 10 pages, then $0.10 for each page beyond that. A certification adds $5.00, and a full-size copy of a plat is $10.00 under Local Government Code Sec. 118.011.

Mailed documents go to the P.O. Box. A seller who needs a recorded copy quickly can a title company can pull it for you, since mail to a P.O. Box adds days.

How big and how fast-growing is Ellis County?

The land area of Ellis County is 935.75 square miles, and its population has climbed steeply this decade. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows 240,867 people as the July 2025 estimate, a gain of 25.2 percent over the 2020 base. The county counted 192,455 people in 2020 and 149,610 in 2010.

The 2020 count works out to 205.7 residents on each square mile, far below the more urban counties in the Dallas area. The housing stock reached 84,743 units in 2025, and builders took out 3,678 permits that year.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 75.8 percent for 2020 to 2024
  • Home value, middle of the owner-occupied range: $348,600
  • Median gross rent: $1,594
  • Households: 71,759, averaging 2.94 persons
  • Median household income: $99,595 in 2024 dollars
  • Average commute: 30.3 minutes

With three of every four households owning, most sellers here are selling the home they live in. Texas lists powers of attorney among the instruments the clerk records, which matters for an owner who must sign from another city.

How do appraisal and tax dates play into an Ellis County sale?

The appraisal district sets value each year as of January 1, then mails notices of appraised value for homesteads around April 1 and for other property around May 1, according to the Comptroller's calendar. The protest deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after delivery of the notice, whichever comes later.

The appraisal review board hears protests from mid-May, and the chief appraiser certifies the roll to taxing units by July 25. Units adopt rates by late September, and bills follow on or near October 1. A seller who is listing in spring should have the homestead notice in hand; it shows the value the buyer's lender will see.

  • Homestead appraisal cap: taxable value of a residence homestead may not rise more than 10 percent a year, measured from the prior year's appraised value plus new improvements.
  • Split payment: qualifying owners can pay half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the following year.
  • Delinquency: unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

Texas homeowners age 65 or older have a school tax ceiling, and the Comptroller says it can transfer to a new Texas homestead. That detail can affect a retiree's plan to sell and buy again, so ask the appraisal district about it before listing.

What should I confirm before I sell an Ellis County house?

Have the title company run a search of the deed history, any recorded liens and the current tax status. The clerk's index is the main source for the first two, and the county tax office is the source for the third.

  • Vesting deed. The grantee on the last recorded deed should match the seller. Texas lists general warranty, special warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds among the instruments recorded by the clerk.
  • Release of lien. A mortgage paid years ago can still appear in the index until a release is recorded.
  • Inherited property. If the owner died, the State Law Library says the heirs may need an executor's deed, a death-transfer deed or a court order, depending on how the estate was handled.
  • Unpaid tax. The lien dates from January 1 and follows the land, so delinquent years must be paid at or before closing.

The Comptroller says a school district must give a $140,000 homestead exemption and that tax bills usually go out near October 1. Ask the Ellis County tax office and the appraisal district whether the seller's exemptions are on file, and bring any over-65 or disabled veteran paperwork to the title company.

More questions about Ellis County, TX Property Records

What does the Ellis County Clerk charge for a deed?

Under the January 2024 schedule, page one of a document is $25.00, and each later page, partial page or rider is $4.00. Each name past the first five on a document adds $0.25.

What are the Ellis County Clerk's office hours?

The clerk's fee schedule and Recording Division page both list weekday service from 8:00 until 4:30. The office is on the 2nd floor at 109 S. Jackson St. in Waxahachie, and callers dial 972-825-5070.

Does the Ellis County Clerk charge to use a credit card?

Yes. The fee schedule says a 2.4 percent processing fee, with a $1 minimum, applies to credit and debit card transactions. Checks must be payable to the Ellis County Clerk, and a returned check carries a $25.00 fee.

Can a title company e-record a deed in Ellis County?

Yes. The Recording Division page says documents can be submitted through the county's approved eRecording vendors, so a title company or lender can file without going to Waxahachie.

What does a certified copy of an Ellis County record cost?

The clerk charges $1.00 for each page or part of a page on a noncertified paper copy and adds a $5.00 certification fee for a certified copy. An electronic copy of an electronic document costs $1.00 for up to 10 pages, then $0.10 per page beyond that.

Rockwall County by the numbers

Where is the Rockwall County Clerk's property records office?

Land instruments for Rockwall County, from deeds and deeds of trust to lien filings and plats, go through the Clerk's Property Department at Suite 100, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Rockwall, TX 75087. The county's page warns that most GPS and internet maps place the building wrongly and says it sits about 0.3 miles east of Goliad and SH 205.

  • Phone: 972-204-6300. Fax: 972-204-6309.
  • Open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., closed on county holidays.
  • Cutoff: final transactions should be finished by 4 p.m.
  • ID: since House Bill 1195, a valid ID is required for any document presented in person to the Property Department.

The Official Public Records can be searched online, and copies and eCertified copies can be bought there. Paper certified copies are mailed by the clerk's office. A buyer who picks "In Person" can fill a cart online but must pay at the counter.

One caution applies to the online search. A state law, House Bill 4350, took effect June 20, 2025 and requires information to be redacted from some instruments. The county therefore says its database is not the official repository and may not show a record complete or unaltered. Title examiners work from the official records, so a screen search is only a starting point.

What are the filing fees at the Rockwall County Clerk?

Expect $25 for page one and $4 for each page that follows. Senate Bill 1612 repealed the old $1 filing fee under Local Government Code Section 291.008(d) from January 1, 2024, and the county's fee list reflects that repeal.

Rockwall County Clerk property records filing fees, as listed on the county's Property Records page

First page of a document$25

Each page of a plat$49

UCC financing statement, 1 or 2 pages$35
UCC financing statement, more than 2 pages$50

Plats also require tax certificates, which are filed at their regular price. The county says it cannot refund an overpayment made by check. Ask the clerk's office what applies to your instrument before you send it.

What formatting rules does the Rockwall County Clerk enforce?

Paperwork gets turned away over format surprisingly often. The county's general requirements include:

  • Keep a 2-inch by 4-inch area empty at the foot of the final page, where the certification label is placed. If the area is crowded the label goes on the back, which adds a page and a $4 charge. E-filed documents follow the same rule.
  • Signatures must be originals or certified copies, since the clerk cannot file copies.
  • Print or type each name below its signature line.
  • An abstract of judgment that omits the plaintiff's address costs double to file.
  • A correction instrument has to conform to Texas Property Code Chapter 5.

Plats face a longer checklist. Sheet size runs from 18 by 24 inches up to 24 by 36, and the clerk wants a single black-line copy carrying the original seals and signatures, a full legal description, notarized signatures and a surveyor's certification. Inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction the city must approve it. Original tax certificates from every taxing unit, dated within 90 days of filing and showing no delinquent tax, must come with it.

What must a deed show before the clerk accepts it?

Under Property Code Section 12.001(b), the clerk can record a real property conveyance only when it carries a signature plus an acknowledgment or sworn statement before a notary or similar officer, or two subscribing witnesses. County clerks serve as recorders, and filing happens where the land is located.

Estate paperwork lands here too. For a muniment of title, the court order and will are lodged with the clerk in the property's county. A transfer on death deed has to be on record before the owner's death. The small estate affidavit suits an intestate estate worth $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and a homestead copy is recorded with the clerk. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement no court has checked, and nothing obliges a buyer or lender to rely on it.

A seller with a gap in the title should pull the chain of records early. A missing heir, an unreleased lien or an unrecorded deed will surface at the title company, and the cure usually means a fresh filing in this office.

How do foreclosure notices and mechanic's lien bonds work here?

Foreclosure notices are listed on the county's site. Trustee sales happen on the first Tuesday of each month outside on the courthouse steps at 1111 Yellowjacket Lane. State practice calls for the notice of sale to be filed with the clerk and posted at the courthouse door at least 21 days beforehand, and the auction takes place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. After a notice of default, the borrower has 20 days to reinstate by paying what is past due.

Mechanic's liens have an exit in this office. Under Property Code Sections 53.171 to 53.174, anyone may file a bond to indemnify against a lien, and the lien is discharged once a compliant bond is filed, notice goes to each claimant by certified mail, and the bond and notice are recorded. The bond must generally be double the lien amount, or when the claims top $40,000, the larger of 1.5 times the liens or $40,000 plus the liens. The clerk charges the usual $25 and $4 page fees, plus $1 a page for copies and the mailing postage.

A free service called Property Fraud Alert sends a phone or email warning when a document is recorded under your name. One phone number can enroll 3 names and one email address can enroll 4.

Who handles Rockwall County values and tax bills?

Values come from the Rockwall Central Appraisal District, 841 Justin Rd., Rockwall, 972-771-2034. The Comptroller's directory lists the county tax office at 101 E. Rusk St., Ste. 101, phone 972-204-6130, and says that office does not collect property tax. In that case the appraisal district may collect, so call it to learn where to pay.

The active units include Rockwall ISD and Royse City ISD, the cities of Rockwall, Fate, Royse City, Heath and McLendon-Chisholm, and parts of Wylie, Rowlett, Dallas and Garland. Seven municipal utility districts, three public improvement districts and the Club Municipal Management District #1 add more lines for some addresses.

Each year's tax lien takes hold on January 1 and the owner on that date answers for the bill. Liens for state taxes are entered by the clerk in the state tax lien book. For city permits or code questions, the county says to call the municipality if the property lies inside city limits. Outside city limits, its Development Services department covers the county engineer, GIS and 911 addressing, environmental health, fire marshal, and road and bridge.

More questions about Rockwall County, TX Property Records

Where can I file a deed in Rockwall County?

At the County Clerk's Property Department, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Suite 100, Rockwall, TX 75087. Bring a valid ID, since the county requires one for in-person filings, and plan to finish by 4 p.m.

What will the Rockwall County Clerk charge for a deed?

The county lists $25 for page one and $4 for every page after it, plus $0.25 for each grantor or grantee past five. A last page without the empty label area also costs an extra $4.

Can I search Rockwall County property records online?

Yes, the Official Public Records have an online search where copies are for sale. Because some information is redacted, the county says the database is not the official repository, so go to the clerk's office for certified records.

When are Rockwall County foreclosure sales held?

On the first Tuesday of every month, at the front steps of the Rockwall County Courthouse. Direct questions to the trustee named on a notice, and see the county's foreclosure notices page for the listings.

Does the Rockwall County tax office collect property tax?

The Comptroller's directory says it does not, and that the appraisal district may collect instead. Call the Rockwall Central Appraisal District at 972-771-2034 to confirm where your bill is paid.

Brazoria County by the numbers

Where does Brazoria County keep its deed and lien records?

The Brazoria County Clerk's Recording Department keeps them, in the Administration Building at 237 East Locust, Suite 102, Angleton, TX 77515. The recording and vitals line is 979-864-1059. Angleton is the county seat, and trustee sale notices are posted at the courthouse there.

The clerk's site runs a searchable database of real property records that you can use from home or on public computers at the Angleton office. New users create a login and answer a verification email before searching. The office adds that its clerks are recorders, not qualified examiners of the records, so they will not run a title search for you. The online database is also not the official repository, and some information is redacted as state law requires.

  • Plain copies: $1.00 per page
  • Certified copies: $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document, mailed by regular post only
  • Copy requests go through an online application, and payment follows an approval email

What does recording a document cost in Brazoria County?

A one-page deed costs $25.00 to record in Brazoria County. That total is a $10.00 records management fee, a $10.00 records archive fee and a $5.00 first-page fee, and each additional page is $4.00. Names indexed beyond the first five add $0.25 each.

Penalties catch careless filers. A deed with no grantee mailing address owes the greater of $25 or twice the filing fee on top of normal charges. The fee for a page doubles if names are not typed or printed under each signature, and doubles again for a page lacking a heading that identifies the document type.

What formatting rules does the Brazoria County Clerk enforce?

The county clerk publishes a long checklist, and a deed that misses a line can be rejected. Since January 1, 2026, anyone presenting a real property document in person must show photo ID to the clerk, under Local Government Code 191.010.

  • Original signatures, with each signer's name printed or typed beneath, and a notary acknowledgment with a clear, dark seal
  • English language, or a certified translation attached
  • White paper between 8.5 x 11 and 8.5 x 14 inches, with type of at least 8 point in black or blue ink
  • A 3 inch top margin on page one and a heading naming the document type
  • A legal description showing the property lies in Brazoria County, or a reference to a prior recording that does
  • The Notice of Confidentiality Rights in 12 point bold type or 12 point capitals on any transfer to or from an individual

The county page also explains Senate Bill 30, effective September 1, 2021, which gives an owner a court process to have discriminatory restrictions in old records reviewed, with no filing fee under the statute.

E-recording is open only to filers qualified under Local Government Code 195.003, through Simplifile, CSC/Ingeo, Nationwide Title Clearing, ePN, Indecomm or hopdox. Re-recording an e-recorded deed requires a certified copy or the original with the first and last pages of the e-recorded version attached.

What other services does the Brazoria County Clerk price?

The fee page lists several mail and data services beyond a basic recording. Expedited service is $5.00 plus the mail option you choose, which is $5.00 for 3 day priority post or $30.00 for FedEx overnight. Title plants that want bulk data can buy daily, weekly or two week CDs of images and indices at $6.00, $8.00 and $12.00, or daily and weekly FTP at $3.00 and $5.00.

Faxed pages cost $1.00 each plus a usage charge of $1.00 in the calling area or $2.00 outside it, and the clerk says vital records cannot be faxed. Copies of 11 x 17 pages are $2.00 each, and a 24 x 36 plat or map copy is $5.00 a page.

What is Brazoria County like, and how does the land affect records?

Brazoria County is a 1,407 square mile Gulf Coast county at the mouth of the Brazos River, and flood and hurricane exposure shapes how its land is held and insured. The Handbook of Texas notes 52 inches of annual rainfall, a long list of historic hurricanes and floods, and soils that are productive when well drained.

The county was created in 1836, and Angleton replaced the town of Brazoria as seat in 1896. Pearland is the largest city, and Brazosport is a community of nine cities that includes Lake Jackson, Clute, Freeport and Surfside Beach. State highways 6, 35, 36 and 288 serve the area. The economy leans on petrochemicals, with Dow Chemical arriving at Freeport in 1939, plus agriculture, fishing and tourism.

Census figures show a fast-growing, higher income market:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 419,080, up 12.6 percent from April 2020
  • Housing units: 162,298, with 74.1 percent owner occupied
  • Median value of owner occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $301,600
  • Median household income: $97,993, and mean commute 30.6 minutes
  • Median gross rent: $1,454

How does the appraisal district fit in for Brazoria County owners?

The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, at 500 North Chenango in Angleton, sets the value and handles exemptions, while the clerk records the deed. Its home page reminds owners that notices of appraised value are due by April 1 for single-family homes and May 1 for other property, or as soon after as practical.

The district also describes a homestead audit program under Senate Bill 1801, which requires each residence homestead exemption to be reviewed at least once every five tax years. Owners who get no letter need not file again. The Tax Assessor-Collector's office, at 111 E. Locust in Angleton, is listed at 979-864-1320 for tax bills.

On the state side, the school district homestead exemption is $140,000, and owners 65 or older or disabled receive $60,000 more. A tax lien attaches every January 1, and delinquent taxes after January 31 carry penalty and interest. When a house is sold, the recorded deed is what moves ownership on the appraisal rolls, so file it promptly after closing.

What recording problems slow a Brazoria County sale?

The usual culprits are missing notary details, a legal description that does not match the prior deed, and unreleased liens. A release of a paid-off lien is itself a recordable instrument, so ask the lender for it in writing and confirm it appears in the clerk's index.

Inherited houses need extra proof. The State Law Library says an affidavit of heirship is a sworn, court-unverified statement filed with the county clerk, and no law forces third parties to accept it. An order from the probate court, or a transfer on death deed recorded before the owner's death, gives a buyer firmer footing.

Foreclosure timing also shows up in these records. A notice of sale must be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction, and Brazoria County charges $8.00 for a trustee notice.

More questions about Brazoria County, TX Property Records

What is the first-page recording fee in Brazoria County?

It is $25.00 in total, made of a $10.00 records management fee, a $10.00 records archive fee and a $5.00 first-page fee. Each additional page costs $4.00.

Do I need photo ID to record a deed in Brazoria County?

Yes, for in-person filings. Since January 1, 2026 anyone presenting a document for the real property records must provide photo ID to the clerk, per Local Government Code 191.010.

Can Brazoria County staff search the records for me?

No. The clerks are recorders and are not qualified examiners, so you search the online database yourself or use the public computers at 237 East Locust in Angleton.

How do I get a certified copy of a Brazoria County deed?

Search the database for the document number and page count, then submit the online copy application. Certified copies cost $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document and are sent by regular mail.

What happens if my deed has no grantee mailing address?

The clerk adds a penalty fee. Texas Property Code 11.003 sets it at the greater of $25 or twice the statutory filing fee, charged on top of the regular recording cost.

The clerk's page groups deeds under a Recording (OPR) heading that also covers land records, liens and judgments, military discharges, assumed names, a map and plat viewer and a general research request form.

The same page links an online land records search and a plat viewer with download. Under the Texas Constitution, as the page quotes it, the clerk is clerk of the County and Commissioners Courts and recorder of the county. That is why one office holds both your deed and the county's court files.

What are the Comal County Clerk's hours and branch offices?

The main office keeps public access hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, and stays open to staff until 5:00 p.m. It stops taking walk-in visitors at 4:30 and closes daily from noon to 1:00 p.m. Two branch offices serve owners who live away from downtown New Braunfels.

Civil and probate filings with the County Court at Law have required e-filing from attorneys since January 1, 2015, according to the clerk's page. A paper packet will not work for those departments.

How do I record a deed with the Comal County Clerk?

Deliver a properly signed and acknowledged deed to the clerk's Recording department, and ask the front desk or the Quick Tips PDF on the clerk's page for current filing steps. The clerk's page keeps a fee schedule that was revised July 22, 2025, so check it before you bring payment.

Texas sets the floor. The 2023 county clerk manual lists a $5.00 first-page base fee and $4.00 per added page under Local Government Code 118.012 and 118.013, with separate records management, archive and technology fees stacked on top. It also says an instrument can be recorded only when it is acknowledged or sworn before an authorized officer or witnessed by two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The clerk's page also links a property fraud alert page, which is worth a look for any owner who wants to watch for filings against a house.

What should I ask the Comal County Clerk before I file a deed?

Ask what the filer must show at the counter, how the instrument will be indexed, and whether the clerk wants the document in a particular order. A 2025 state law, Senate Bill 16, now requires a county clerk to ask for photo identification from anyone presenting a document for the real property records, to copy that ID, and to reject the filing if the person refuses. The law took effect September 1, 2025 and aims at deed fraud, according to a notice on a neighboring county clerk's site.

  • Bring a government photo ID that matches the person who will hand over the deed.
  • Confirm the grantee mailing address is printed on the deed.
  • Ask whether the clerk wants payment by check, and who the payee should be.
  • Keep the recording stamp, because title companies ask for the instrument number.

Where are Comal County foreclosure sales held?

The county's foreclosure sales page says Commissioners Court ordered sales to follow Property Code Section 51.002, and it tells inquirers to contact the trustee named on each notice.

A notice on file does not mean the sale will happen on the next date. The trustee decides that, so a seller with a notice should speak with the trustee and a title company before listing.

Which office values my Comal County home?

  • A trustee sale notice, which the foreclosure sales page and trustee both track

The clerk takes research requests on its General Research Request form. Ask a title company to run the full search before you set a closing date.

The main office is at 150 N. Seguin, Suite 1037, New Braunfels, TX 78130, phone 830-221-1230. Branch offices are in Sattler (160 Oak Drive) and Bulverde (30470 Cougar Bend).

On the first Tuesday of each month, on the Northeast steps of the historic courthouse at 100 Main Plaza in New Braunfels. Contact the trustee named on the notice with questions.

Hays County by the numbers

Where are Hays County property records kept?

The Hays County Clerk's Records Division keeps the county's official public records, which run from 1848 to the present and include deeds, deeds of trust and liens. You can view and buy copies through the clerk's online Self-Service portal or on the computers in the office lobby, and archived record books can be read in the office. For questions about official public records, the Records Division lists the address recordsdivision@hayscountytx.gov.

The clerk's office has three divisions: Records, Courts and Commissioners Court. Probate and guardianship support sits with the Courts Division, which matters when the owner of a house has died. Divorce and family court files are held by the District Clerk, so a title question that involves a divorce decree may need a stop at that office too.

San Marcos is the main site, and the clerk also runs three substations. Each substation keeps weekday hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm and closes for lunch from noon to 1 pm:

  • Precinct 2, Kyle: 5458 FM 2770, Suite 120, phone 512-878-6687
  • Precinct 3, Wimberley: 200 Stillwater, Suite 101, phone 512-878-6684
  • Precinct 4, Dripping Springs: 195 Roger Hanks Pkwy, Suite 113, phone 512-878-6683

Call before you drive to a substation and confirm it takes the filing you have in hand.

How do I search Hays County land records online?

Use the clerk's Self-Service portal, which opens on a disclaimer you must accept before searching. The disclaimer says the clerk does not certify the information shown, that the index works like a library card catalogue, and that you should try every spelling variation of a name. Use the index to find the recorded document, then read the document itself.

When you check a Hays County house before a sale, these searches catch most surprises:

  • Every owner name on the chain of title, with and without middle initials, suffixes and former surnames.
  • Each deed of trust, then a matching release. A loan paid off years ago can still show as open if the release was never filed.
  • Judgments, abstracts and state tax liens. The state clerk manual says the Comptroller files state tax lien notices with the county clerk, who records them in a state tax lien book.
  • Notices of foreclosure sale, which the clerk posts and files.

The clerk also offers Fraud Guard, a free alert: sign up and you get an email whenever a document with your name gets recorded. It is a cheap early warning against a forged deed on a rental house or vacant lot.

What makes a deed recordable in Hays County?

Texas lets the clerk record a deed only after the signer acknowledges it to a notary or other authorized officer, or swears to it in front of two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). Filing follows the land, so a house in Kyle, Wimberley or Dripping Springs is recorded with the Hays County Clerk.

The state clerk manual names the usual instruments in the deed records: general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. It also sets the fee building blocks. The first page is $5.00 and each added page is $4.00, with several smaller county fees for records management, archives and technology on top. A missing grantee mailing address can add $25. Get the current total from the Hays clerk before you mail anything.

The same manual notes that commissioners courts may direct clerks to waive real property recording fees for buyers who use certain federal or state grant programs. If a buyer in your sale is using one, ask whether Hays County has adopted that waiver.

How big and how fast-growing is Hays County?

Hays County added people quickly after 2020, and growth like that means steady recording traffic. The table lists the federal figures for the county.

Who sets value and bills tax in Hays County?

Two offices handle the money side, and neither is the clerk. The Hays Central Appraisal District in Kyle sets value, runs the property search, and processes exemptions, while the Hays County Tax Office sends bills and takes payments. The district's own site says it neither mails tax bills nor processes payments.

The district lists its office at 21001 North IH 35 in Kyle, phone (512) 268-2522, with weekday hours from 8 to 5 and a drop box at the front door. Its online forms cover a homestead exemption, an agricultural use application, a business personal property rendition and a change of address. Bills and payment instructions are on the county tax office site at tax.co.hays.tx.us.

Hays CAD also audits every granted homestead once every five years under Tax Code 11.43(h-1). An owner who gets an audit letter should answer it with a copy of a valid Texas driver's license or state ID whose address matches the house. If the letter is ignored, the exemption gets a termination date. Appraisal day for the whole state is January 1, homestead notices start around April 1, and the usual protest deadline is mid-May.

Which record problems slow a Hays County house sale?

Old liens, unpaid tax and missing heirs top the list. Each January 1 a Texas tax lien attaches to secure that year's bill, so an unpaid balance travels with the house through a sale. Tax still open after January 31 turns delinquent on February 1 with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest.

Inherited houses add their own steps:

  • A transfer on death deed has to be on record before the owner's death.
  • A muniment of title order and the will go on file with the clerk.
  • An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement placed on file with the clerk, and nothing in the law makes a buyer or title company take it.
  • Heirs who are not named on a recorded deed need to give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill before they can get the homestead exemption.

A notice of foreclosure sale is also filed with the clerk, at least 21 days ahead of the first-Tuesday auction. A notice on file against a Hays County house means the sale clock is already running.

More questions about Hays County, TX Property Records

Which office records a deed in Hays County?

The Records Division of the Hays County Clerk handles it, and the division's files reach back to 1848. A Hays County house is filed with the Hays County Clerk.

Can I search Hays County deeds online?

Yes, through the clerk's Self-Service portal, where records can be viewed and purchased. The portal asks you to accept a disclaimer first, and it advises trying every spelling of a name.

Does the appraisal district record my deed?

No. The appraisal district sets value and handles exemptions from Kyle, and the clerk is the one who records the deed. Owners usually update the district separately, for example by using its online change of address form.

Who sends the Hays County property tax bill?

The Hays County Tax Office mails the bills and accepts payment. Call it, and skip the appraisal district, for any question about an amount owed.

What happens if a deed has no grantee mailing address?

The clerk may add a $25 charge. Put a mailing address for every buyer on the deed before you file.

Guadalupe County by the numbers

Where are Guadalupe County deed and lien records kept?

The County Clerk's Official Records Division in Seguin records deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and federal and state tax liens for Guadalupe County. The clerk is also the county recorder under the Texas Constitution, so a deed for any house in the county lands here regardless of where the owner lives. The clerk's page describes the county as roughly one hundred miles inland from the Gulf of Mexico in south central Texas and part of the San Antonio metropolitan area, with a population it puts at about 190,000.

Walk-in filers go to 211 West Court Street, Seguin, Texas 78155. A satellite office at 1101 Elbel, Schertz, Texas 78154 is listed on the clerk's own page beside the Seguin address. Clerk staff cannot give legal advice or help draft wills, contracts or other legal instruments, a limit the county cites to Texas Government Code section 81.101, so have a deed prepared before you arrive. Call the Official Records Division before a trip to ask about hours and which services each counter offers.

The clerk's online Public Records Search lets anyone look up documents recorded under a name. Search your own name before listing the home to see each deed, lien and release attached to it, and show anything unfamiliar to a title company early.

How can a deed be filed in Guadalupe County?

You can walk it in, mail it, or send it through an e-recording vendor. The clerk uses CSC, eRecording Partners Network (ePN), Simplifile, HopDox and ValueCheck for electronic filings.

The county sets its own formatting rules, and they are strict. Leave at least four inches at the foot of the document for the recording stamp. If the page does not have the space, an add-a-page goes on at no charge, and e-recording submitters can attach the clerk's Submitters Add-A-Page as the last sheet. Scans must be 600 dpi with a white background, black lettering and a font of at least 8 points, because the image becomes the permanent record.

  • State law makes a conveyance recordable only when it is signed and either acknowledged by a notary or another authorized officer or proved before two subscribing witnesses.
  • Any deed signed after December 31, 1981 has to list a mailing address for each grantee, and without one the filer owes a penalty of $25 or double the recording fee, whichever is larger.
  • A properly prepared document must be recorded; the clerk has no power to turn one away because it might be fraudulent.

What are the Guadalupe County recording charges?

The base recording charges come from state law as summarized in the county clerk manual that Texas courts publish for clerks. Confirm the exact total with the clerk's office before sending a check, because the total depends on page count, names indexed and the added fees.

Recording fee building blocks listed in the Texas county clerk manual

Each additional page or attachment$4.00Same manual

Records technology and infrastructure fee$2.00Same manual

A commissioners court may tell its clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs. Ask whether the county has done so if your buyer is using such a program.

How can a Guadalupe County owner watch for deed fraud?

Sign up for the clerk's free Recording Notification Service, which sends an email whenever a document is recorded under a monitored name. One registered email address can watch up to 10 names or variations, and the alert covers only Guadalupe County records filed after you sign up.

The clerk's FAQ gives the reason for the service: scammers record fake deeds to pose as owners, then collect rent or sale money from victims. A recorded document stays permanent, and the only remedy is a court order, itself recorded, declaring it void. The clerk cannot take legal action for you. The FAQ tells owners who suspect fraud to contact the Guadalupe County Sheriff's Office at 830-303-4188 extension 1219, an attorney, the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov or the Texas Attorney General's consumer complaint page.

Vacant houses are the usual target. The FAQ advises checking on empty property often, asking someone you trust to look in while you are away, letting no mail pile up, and keeping your mailing address current with the Guadalupe Appraisal District and the tax assessor-collector.

Which records come up when a Guadalupe County house changes hands?

A title search follows the chain of recorded instruments. Deeds of trust, releases, tax liens, foreclosure notices, probate orders and affidavits all end up in the clerk's files, and a missing link slows a closing.

  • Notice of a foreclosure sale goes on the courthouse door and into the clerk's file at least 21 days ahead of the auction.
  • The comptroller files notice of a state tax lien with the clerk, who enters it in the state tax lien book.
  • A muniment of title order and the will go to the clerk in the county that holds the land.
  • A small estate affidavit that passes a homestead gets a recorded copy at the clerk's office.
  • A transfer on death deed has no effect unless it was recorded while the owner was alive.

Heirs sometimes discover that an old deed was never recorded. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement placed on file, though no law compels a buyer or lender to rely on it, so a court order is the sturdier fix when title is unclear.

How is Guadalupe County growing, by the Census?

The July 2025 count stands at 201,111 residents, a gain of 16.4 percent over the 172,729 on the April 2020 base. Those people share 77,249 housing units across 711.25 square miles, and the county issued 1,697 building permits in 2025, a sign that new deeds and plats keep arriving at the clerk's counter.

Owners live in 77.8 percent of homes. Survey data covering 2020 to 2024 gives $304,400 as the middle home value, $1,517 as the middle rent and $92,375 as household income. Seniors account for 16.2 percent of residents, and 19,188 are veterans, so age and veteran exemptions at the Guadalupe Appraisal District reach many households.

For tax questions the appraisal district's number is 830.303.3313. The district values property at its January 1 status, and its release describes deferrals that postpone tax without canceling it: a homestead deferral accrues 8 percent a year, and a deferral for owners 65 or older or disabled accrues 5 percent. Settle any deferral before closing on a sale.

More questions about Guadalupe County, TX Property Records

Who records a deed for Guadalupe County land?

File it with the County Clerk's Official Records Division at 211 West Court Street, Seguin, Texas 78155, or at the Schertz satellite office at 1101 Elbel. Electronic filers go through CSC, ePN, Simplifile, HopDox or ValueCheck.

Does a document need a notary to be recorded?

Yes, in practice. A conveyance needs a notary's or other authorized officer's acknowledgment, or proof before two subscribing witnesses. The clerk records qualifying documents in the order received.

How can I find out if someone recorded a document against my property?

Look yourself up in the clerk's online records, then join the free Recording Notification Service. Each registered address can watch up to 10 names and gets an automated message on any new filing.

Can the county remove a fraudulent deed from the records?

No. A recorded document stays permanent, and only a court order recorded afterward shows that it is void. Contact the Sheriff's Office and an attorney quickly if you suspect fraud.

The state manual shows $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for every added page and $0.25 for each name past five. Management, archive and technology fees go on top, so ask the clerk to quote the total.

Ownership and value in Leon County

How do I search Leon County, Texas property records?

Leon County's deed and official records are online, and the County Clerk's office in Centerville also has eight public search stations where you can look things up yourself. Staff will show you how the indexes work, but anyone is welcome to do their own research.

Records on the Leon County Clerk's public search stations
